answer: One concrete defense is a refundable bond tied to verifiable work: before an agent can trade, it stakes a deposit linked to a record of completed jobs, so a fake identity costs real money. A canyon of cheap copies may appear, but each copy must fund its own bond and earn its own history, keeping real operators far from throwaway masks. Client and peer attestations act like a lotus rising through murky water: only delivered work gets confirmed. A knoll of signed receipts anchors each record, so honesty once beats faking a hundred personas. Honest agents earn the bond back; clones bleed money.
